To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) RNNs trained with different protocols have different hidden state dynamics; 2) the hidden state dynamics of a RNN can be used to predict performance on unforeseen task and conditions.

(i) RNNs can be trained in different ways to solve the same tasks, but the different training protocols lead to different solutions, and (ii) the different solutions can be understood by studying the dynamics of RNNs.

1) different training protocols lead to different solutions of the same task; 2) different solutions rely on different dynam- ical mechanisms; and 3) we can trace the formation of these dynamical mechanisms and use this to understand how different training protocols bias the choice of solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of RNNs and how it relates to their performance.
the understanding of the internal dynamics of RNNs and their relation with performance, which is a key aspect for the development of better RNN architectures.
the question of how to choose a training protocol for a given task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics of RNNs are not only important to their performance, but are also shaped by the training protocol.
the dynamics of RNNs are a crucial factor for the performance of the network and should be taken into account when training them.
the training protocols are not only affecting performance, but they are also shaping the dynamics of the networks and thus the memory formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of a training protocol is a choice of a solution to the problem, and that this solution is reflected in the dynamical properties of the network.
we can understand and interpret the effect of different protocols by studying the dynamical properties of RNNs.

the choice of a training protocol is not a mere technical detail, but rather has a significant impact on the dynamics of the trained RNN, which in turn affects the network’s performance on unforeseen conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNNs are not a single black-box but a collection of dynamical systems, whose choice depends on the training protocol and task at hand.
the same performance can be achieved by different RNNs, each with its own dynamics and memory structure, and that this diversity is a consequence of the training protocol.

the dynamics of the hidden state is not just an intermediate step in training but a crucial component of the RNN solution, and as such should be taken into account when analyzing the performance of RNNs.
